text:
andrew: Quick thought — instead of pushing SLA logic down into the policy engine, what if we bake SLA-awareness into the routing adapter itself? It would let the runtime make routing decisions with fewer roundtrips and lower decision latency.

sasha: I'm intrigued. Do you mean move latency/cost/tier weighting into adapters? How would that affect policy testing and audits?

tomas: Concern: duplication of semantics across adapters. We need a compact, well-defined contract so adapters stay replaceable and stateless. Maybe an SLA hint + a tiny scoring function.

evan: ops-bot: can we get probe telemetry for this? :robot_face: 

andrew: Sketch of the idea:
- runtime attaches a tenant SLA vector (p99 target, cost budget, region preferences) to the request
- adapters keep precomputed model/region profiles (latency, cost) and apply a local scoring function
- adapter returns N ranked candidates + reasons/uncertainty so the runtime can still enforce global policy

Example runtime payload (concept):
```json
{"tenant_sla":{"p99_ms":150,"cost_per_m_token_usd":0.0009,"regions":["us-west","eu"]},"input_len":128}
```

sasha: Backwards compatibility is tricky — we can't require tenants to author SLA vectors today.

tomas: Agreed. Migration idea: policy compiler emits SLA hints per route when available. Adapters operate in two modes: legacy (use existing weights) and hint-driven (use SLA hints if present). Defaults cover the rest.

evan: Observability needs to be first-class: every decision should include an explain field + correlation id so we can tie route choices to probe windows and real latency. We'll also want sim-mode to validate decisions before full rollout.

andrew: Proposed rollout plan: 
1) Add optional SLA hint field to policy compiler (no runtime changes initially)
2) Adapter reads hints via a shim and supports sim-mode (no effect on routing)
3) Gradual runtime enablement via env flag + canary tenant list
4) Telemetry gates: decision drift, p99 delta, cost delta thresholds must pass before broad enablement

sasha: Edge cases: bursty tails, KV cache priming, and cold-starts will skew adapter profiles. Adapters should include an "uncertainty" score to represent how confident the profile is.

tomas: API suggestion for adapter response to keep contracts small: 
```json
{"candidates":[{"route":"dedicated-gpu-v2","score":0.82,"reason":"meets p99 & cost","uncertainty":0.12}],"explain":"probe_window=1h","correlation_id":"abc-123"}
```

evan: Ops checklist for rollout: 
- probe windows per region + model variant
- regression alerting for p95/p99
- fallback behavior when no candidate meets SLA :rotating_light:
- simulation harness to check decision parity with legacy router

andrew: +1 to uncertainty + explicit fallback. Keep the runtime's selection logic simple: adapter may return up to N candidates; runtime picks the first candidate where score >= threshold (threshold controlled by runtime config). That keeps determinism at runtime and lets adapters be opinionated.

sasha: I'll draft a short RFC appendix that defines the adapter contract (payloads, sample payloads, uncertainty semantics), and sketch the migration path. Volunteering to take the first pass. @tomas @evan any objections?

tomas: +1. I'll mock up a scoring matrix and run a few sims against the existing router to measure decision drift.

evan: I'll update dashboards and wire alerts for the canary tenants. Ops-bot created incident tracker: #inc-1234

andrew: Nice. If the RFC looks good we can schedule a 30m sync to nail the open questions. :thumbsup:
